statement: Four distinct spheres in R3 have infinitely many real common tangent lines if and only if their centers are collinear and at least one common real tangent exists. Such spheres either intersect in a common circle (possibly a point), or are tangent along circles to one common quadric of revolution whose axis contains all centers; this quadric may be a cone, cylinder or one-sheeted hyperboloid.
